title: Proof
summary: A proof is a finite, checkable chain from admitted premises to a conclusion under declared rules.

context.note: This node belongs to one explicit foundational presentation; alternate foundations may encode it differently.

assumptions.text: The declared formal proof system context is fixed.

content.plain: A proof is a finite, checkable chain from admitted premises to a conclusion under declared rules.
content.exact: An S-proof of P from Γ is a finite sequence of formulas ending in P, each of which is an axiom, an admitted premise, or follows from earlier formulas by an S-rule.
content.example: A two-line derivation may use P and P→Q to conclude Q by modus ponens.
content.caveat: A persuasive explanation and a formal derivation serve different purposes; QEVA can link both without calling them identical.
